answer-para2.content: Batching requests improves GPU utilisation during LLM inference primarily because GPUs are massively parallel processors that achieve their peak performance when processing many operations simultaneously, rather than a few at a time. When you serve requests one at a time, the GPU spends a significant portion of its time idle or waiting, because each individual inference involves relatively small matrix operations that cannot fully occupy the thousands of compute cores available. By grouping multiple requests together into a batch, you create larger tensor operations that keep all the GPU cores busy, dramatically increasing throughput and reducing the average latency per request. Additionally, batching amortises the fixed overhead associated with each inference, such as kernel launch costs and memory management operations, across many requests at once. This is especially important during the prefill phase, where the model processes the entire input prompt in a single large computation, versus the decoding phase, where tokens are generated one at a time. Modern inference frameworks use techniques like continuous batching to further improve utilisation by combining new requests with those still being decoded, ensuring the GPU remains saturated with work for as much of the time as possible.
